math_plain: Measure fairness bias in language models across languages and cultures by evaluating their predictions against curated benchmarks.
why_math: Comparing model outputs to known bias categories reveals systematic patterns in how models learn from their training data, separating genuine model failures from language-specific challenges.

math_tags: learning a function from examples
finding the settings with least error
math_plain: Learn flexible alignment rules between recommendation domains using few examples, then replay refined data to reduce transfer mistakes.
why_math: By adjusting how knowledge transfers based on overlapping examples, the model avoids rigid alignment rules that fail in new scenarios and catches negative transfer before it harms recommendations.

math_tags: learning by comparison of similar and different
finding the settings with least error
math_plain: Select negative examples strategically when training graph classifiers, choosing cases that meaningfully distinguish true relationships from false ones.
why_math: A model trained on hard negative cases learns the boundary between real and missing edges more sharply than random negatives, so it generalizes better to unseen edges.

math_tags: finding the settings with least error
measuring similarity as nearness in a space
math_plain: Stabilize item embeddings during federated training by minimizing loss at points least likely to overfit when data distributions change.
why_math: Embeddings that remain robust when slightly perturbed generalize to new users because they exploit stable relationships rather than brittle local patterns in training data.

math_tags: spreading information across a network
smart random sampling and averaging
math_plain: Decide which web pages to recrawl using graph structure and learned probabilities, prioritizing updates that cascade to many downstream pages.
why_math: When one page changes, its outbound links matter more than random updates because information flows through those connections, so prioritizing them keeps the graph fresher with fewer crawls.

math_plain: Train a chatbot to correct misinformation by learning correction strategies, then measure how well it reduces false belief across health, science, and politics domains.
why_math: Testing across unrelated domains reveals whether the model learned general error-correction principles or domain-specific tricks, showing if its approach generalizes or needs retuning.

math_plain: Build a tree of subquestions, score each node's confidence, then prune branches with low confidence and retrieve only entity-level anchors needed for reasoning.
why_math: Confidence-guided pruning keeps only branches that retrieve truly useful evidence, reducing noise that would otherwise dilute the model's ability to combine facts into correct answers.

math_tags: spreading information across a network

math_plain: Detect anomalies in graphs with multiple node types by aligning semantic features across types and weighting their contributions to balance sparse and rich nodes.
why_math: Nodes of different types carry unequal anomaly signals; weighting by reliability spreads discriminative cues from informative nodes to sparse ones, surfacing anomalies that cross type boundaries.

math_plain: Answer student questions and assess engagement by retrieving relevant educational content and personalized context from a learner's history.
why_math: Pulling in retrieved context prevents the model from forgetting prior interactions, so it can recognize when a question connects to earlier topics and tailor answers to that student's level.

math_plain: Train large models on diverse structured data tasks simultaneously so they learn universal patterns that work across recommendation, forecasting, and user behavior prediction.
why_math: Multi-task pretraining exploits patterns common to all structured prediction—ranking importance, spotting relationships, handling missingness—so the model transfers these insights to new tasks without retraining.

math_plain: Evaluate whether chatbots remember fragmented user disclosures across sessions, extract implicit needs, spot conflicts, and personalize support over time.
why_math: Emotional support requires the model to reconstruct a coherent user profile from scattered hints, so measuring these capabilities separately reveals which memory failures break personalization.

math_plain: Edit image emotions by aligning semantic emotion changes while preserving emotion-neutral content through contrasting paired image versions.
why_math: Comparing before and after helps the model learn which features control emotion versus which are incidental, so it can shift one while keeping the rest intact.

math_plain: Enrich sparse user-item graphs by adding intent nodes that summarize shared behavioral patterns, then align users and items consistently across multiple views.
why_math: Intent nodes capture latent reasons why users like items; aligning across views forces the model to agree on these hidden intents, stabilizing recommendations when edges are sparse.

math_plain: Generate relevant documents for conversational search by denoising conversation context with logic, then learning which prior turns matter most for each turn.
why_math: Not all conversation history helps equally; weighting turns by logical coherence and relevance ensures the model attends to clarifying context while ignoring off-topic digressions.

matching and allocating who gets what
math_plain: Map user goals in plain language to relevant UI components by scoring which functions best match the intent, then assemble them into a custom interface.
why_math: Scoring component relevance to goals focuses the interface on what matters for this task, reducing cognitive load by hiding irrelevant options that clutter traditional navigation menus.
